o1.biggest_strength: It understands the two biggest launch risks: retained users come from creators/community, and the migration problem can swamp support if we do not gate it before launch.
o1.biggest_mistake: The channel ranking is muddled: it says it ranks by users who stay, but puts extension authors ahead of X and Product Hunt below Hacker News despite the retained-user math.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the retained-user ranking, tighten the rollout/support plan so it fits the small team, and make the go/no-go criteria a little more practical while keeping the strong messaging drafts.

o2.biggest_strength: It puts the right bets first: YouTube creators, extension authors, migration safety, staged rollout, support capacity, and clear no-go rules before the code freeze.
o2.biggest_mistake: The migration gate is too soft at 95%; for our audience, losing hotkeys for even a small group is launch-blocking unless the issue is fixed, not just documented.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make migration carry-over a stricter gate, add a little more detail to the author/creator launch assets, and sharpen the launch email with named community credits once available.

reason: I would hand Output 2 to the team tomorrow with fewer changes. It makes the right strategic call to delay low-retention channels, stage the risky existing-user rollout, and focus our limited team on creators, authors, and migration support.
